lead.t: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia (AML) is marked by the accumulation of immature myeloid blasts in the bone marrow and often involves specific genetic mutations, with Acute Promyelocytic Leukaemia being notably responsive to targeted differentiation therapy.

qs.q: During the morphological assessment of a bone marrow aspirate from a patient with acute myeloid leukaemia, pathognomonic pink needle-like cytoplasmic inclusions are identified within the myeloblasts. What are these structures called?
o: C. Dacrocytes found in primary myelofibrosis
D. Philadelphia chromosomes found in chronic myeloid leukaemia
A. Auer rods found in acute myeloid leukaemia
B. Smudge cells found in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia
qs.e: Auer rods are pathognomonic pink needle-like cytoplasmic inclusions found in myeloblasts in acute myeloid leukaemia. Smudge cells are fragile lymphocytes characteristic of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia.
qs.s: Acute Leukaemia (AML/ALL) & WBC Disorders: Haematology Guide: MCQs

qs.q: What is the ultimate curative treatment option available for eligible and fit patients diagnosed with a myelodysplastic syndrome that carries a high risk of progression to acute myeloid leukaemia?
qs.e: Allogeneic stem cell transplantation is the only curative option for eligible and fit patients with myelodysplastic syndromes, offering the benefit of a graft-versus-tumour effect. Azacitidine is a hypomethylating agent used in management, but it is not typically considered curative on its own.
qs.s: Haematology & Blood Transfusion Pathology: MDS, Stem Cell Transplant: MCQs

qs.q: A 62-year-old man presents with fatigue, fever and bruising. His full blood count shows WCC 40×10⁹/L with 25% circulating blasts, Hb 90 g/L and platelets 50×10⁹/L. Which investigation is required to definitively diagnose acute myeloid leukaemia?
o: Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy
qs.e: Although the peripheral smear already shows circulating blasts, definitive diagnosis and subclassification of AML require bone marrow examination — combining morphology, cytochemistry, immunophenotyping, and cytogenetic/molecular analysis.

qs.q: In acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), Auer rods are
o: Seen in all acute myeloid subtypes
A sign of chronic myeloid blast crisis
qs.e: Auer rods are fused lysosomal granules forming needle-like inclusions specific to myeloid blasts; their presence confirms AML over ALL.
